priorAttempts.failure: New claim test incorrectly forced OCR preference on the idle follow-up; production implementation was unchanged.

initialAttempt.failure: The mock API returned 429 only on the first request, then allowed other requests before the 50-second reset. At the 48-second observation it had received 6 requests instead of the asserted 1.

correction.correction: Return 429 to every request until the same monotonic 50-second deadline. Allow at most two initial SDK HTTP attempts because bucket discovery can use distinct handlers. All requests observed before the deadline must have received 429; app-level pending SDK calls, attempt count and claimed-owner count retain their original assertions.

performance.claim: Confirmed bounded ownership and reduced SQL wire; no all-condition normal CPU/p95 non-regression claim unless the paired intervals pass.

faultVerification.scenario: 100 second unresolved SDK + blocked actual Pino + two result owners/four accepted receipts/attendance renew/retention
faultVerification.notes: SDK success after application timeout can lead to resending after settlement, according to existing nonce/uncertain-delivery contract.

reviews.round2OutputRecovery: Initial invocation returned a truncated fragment after automatic output continuation; complete stream captured in the repeated invocation of the same review round.

runtimeSourceNote: Only docs/db-rule.md and tests/notifications/receiptPreparation.test.ts changed after the final image source 6c7de44; runtime/build inputs are identical.

rateLimitVerification.scenario: Real @discordjs/rest with loopback HTTP 429, Retry-After 50 seconds, two original SDK Promises and four queued receipts
rateLimitVerification.limitation: No Discord service or Gateway connection. Same-nonce retry after SDK settlement remains allowed; mock API applies nonce deduplication.

gateStatusNote: Code, real DB, runtime image, capacity, bounded fault ownership and shutdown gates passed. Performance comparison is complete with inconclusive normal CPU/zero-RTT p95 and higher invalid-input p95 under RTT20/50; it is not a universal non-regression pass.

method.confidence: 95% two-sided paired t interval on log ratios; 20,000 paired bootstrap draws as sensitivity only
method.decision: Unchanged 1.10 upper-bound threshold; no claim of non-regression when the upper t bound exceeds 1.10
method.statisticalUnit: Independent run pair, not individual notification
method.p95: Two-significant-figure fixed histogram of 20 normal notifications per run; duplicate/invalid each32 requests
method.warmup: 200 notifications at zero injected RTT plus one second natural idle, excluded from CPU/latency window; cgroup peak includes startup/warmup
method.scope: Warm steady-state timing; detailed database diagnostics are retained as a separate study; no cold-start claim
method.errorCounterScope: Control-probe exceptions only; HTTP statuses, delivery counts, maximum attempt and capacity validated separately.

limits: diagnostic async context labeling corrected afterward

limits: periodic full memory sampler still present
stopped because queue deadline defect required a code fix; no results selected by performance

limitations: Each phase has a separate paired interval; there is no simultaneous confidence guarantee across all metrics.
Cgroup peaks include startup and warmup. CPU includes the in-container TCP proxy, real Pino and bounded measurement.
Twenty normal samples per run give a coarse p95. No cold-start, real Discord/Gateway, Neon/TLS or production x64 SLA claim.
All four changes are compared together; isolated wire measurement establishes SQL mechanism, not each candidate's separate total CPU effect.
Existing uncertain-delivery semantics allow same-nonce retry after SDK settlement.
